clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: During an N95 supply shortage, a facility uses the NIOSH contingency strategy called extended use. Which practice is extended use?

options.A: One worker keeps the same N95 on for repeated patient encounters without removing it between encounters.
options.B: One worker removes the same N95 after each encounter and later dons that respirator again.
options.C: Several workers use the same N95 during a shift as long as each performs a seal check.
options.D: One worker continues wearing the same N95 after it is contaminated with patient body fluids.

semantic_correction.rationale: NIOSH defines extended use as wearing the same N95 respirator for repeated close-contact encounters with several different patients without removing the respirator between encounters. Limited reuse differs because the same worker doffs the respirator after an encounter and later dons it again. NIOSH also states that disposable N95 respirators should not be shared among healthcare personnel and that respirators contaminated with blood, respiratory or nasal secretions, or other body fluids should be discarded. Therefore, option A is the only example of extended use.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Distinguish N95 extended use from limited reuse, sharing, and continued use after contamination.
semantic_correction.source_organization: National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH), Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

audit_findings_append.finding: The original concept was accurate but the answer was uniquely longest. The revised item contrasts four concrete respirator-use patterns and preserves NIOSH's exact distinction between extended use and limited reuse.

option_audit.A: Correct. This matches NIOSH's definition of extended use: repeated encounters without removing the respirator between encounters.
option_audit.B: Incorrect but plausible. This is limited reuse because the respirator is doffed and later redonned by the same worker.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. NIOSH states disposable N95 respirators should not be shared among healthcare personnel.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. NIOSH directs disposal when the respirator becomes contaminated with patient body fluids.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone matches the NIOSH definition of extended use; B is explicitly limited reuse and C/D violate stated safety criteria.
cueing_check: All four options describe N95-use patterns of comparable length and structure; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
